key_insight: The paper shows that standard cross-entropy is a “patient” objective that accounts for future learning, and introduces horizon loss to interpolate toward exact policy gradient by truncating the remaining-learning horizon.
engineering_relevance: For classification and LLM-style post-training, horizon loss is a simple drop-in objective that can improve accuracy when label noise or training dynamics make cross-entropy or exact policy gradient suboptimal.
method: Reinterpret classification as a policy-learning problem where expected accuracy is the reward.
Define horizon loss by integrating future error only over the amount of learning that remains.
Show in a simple allocation model that this avoids the failure modes of both cross-entropy and exact policy gradient.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved top-1 accuracy on MNIST and on ImageNet using ResNet-50, ResNet-101, and ViT-S/16, with gains increasing under label noise.
watch_item: The method depends on choosing how much learning horizon remains, so its practical benefit may be sensitive to training schedule and hyperparameter tuning.
